chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others said: Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Khaqan was in charge of the estates and the land-tax in Qumm, and it occurred in...

One day in his gathering, the mention of the 'Alawis and their doctrines came up, and he was intensely hostile toward them. So he said: “I have neither seen nor known in Surra Man Ra'a any man from the 'Alawis like al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Rida in his guidance, composure, chastity, nobility, and generosity, and in the esteem in which his household and Banu Hashim held him, giving him precedence over those among them of greater age and rank; and likewise among commanders, ministers, and the common people.”

For one day I was standing near my father while it was his public audience day, when his doorkeepers entered and said, “Abu Muhammad ibn al-Rida is at the door.” He said loudly, “Give him permission.” I was astonished at what I heard from them, that they dared to address a man by his kunyah before my father in his presence, whereas no one was addressed by kunyah before him except a caliph, an heir apparent, or one whom the ruler had ordered to be so addressed.

Then a dark-complexioned man entered, of fine stature, handsome face, sound body, and young age; he possessed majesty and awe. When my father saw him, he stood and walked a few steps toward him, and I do not know him to have done this for anyone among Banu Hashim or the commanders. When he came near him, he embraced him, kissed his face and chest, took his hand, seated him upon his own prayer-place, sat beside him facing him, and began speaking with him and offering himself in ransom for him.

While I was amazed at what I was seeing from him, the chamberlain entered and said, “Al-Muwaffaq has arrived.” Whenever al-Muwaffaq came to my father, his doorkeepers and elite commanders would precede him and stand in two rows between my father’s sitting place and the door of the house until he entered and departed. Yet my father continued facing Abu Muhammad and speaking with him until he looked toward the private attendants and then said, “Whenever you wish—may Allah make me your ransom.”

Then he said to his doorkeepers, “Take him behind the two rows so that this one—meaning al-Muwaffaq—does not see him.” So he rose, and my father rose, embraced him, and he departed. I said to my father’s doorkeepers and servants, “Woe to you! Who is this man whom you addressed by kunyah before my father, and for whom my father acted in this manner?” They said, “This is an 'Alawi called al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, known as Ibn al-Rida.” My amazement increased, and all that day I remained anxious and reflective about him, my father, and what I had seen, until night came. It was my father’s habit to perform the 'Isha salat (prayer), then sit and review what he needed of administrative affairs and what he would submit to the ruler.

When he had prayed and sat down, I came and sat before him while no one else was with him. He said to me, “O Ahmad, do you have a need?” I said, “Yes, father. If you permit me, I will ask you about it.” He said, “I have permitted you, my son, so say whatever you wish.” I said, “Father, who was the man whom I saw this morning, for whom you showed such veneration, honor, and exaltation, and for whom you offered yourself and your parents in ransom?”

He said, “My son, that is the Imam of the Rafidah; that is al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, known as Ibn al-Rida.” He was silent for a while, then said, “My son, if the Imamate were removed from the caliphs of Banu al-'Abbas, no one from Banu Hashim would deserve it except this man. He indeed deserves it by virtue of his excellence, chastity, guidance, guardedness, asceticism, worship, beautiful character, and righteousness. Had you seen his father, you would have seen a man mighty, noble, and virtuous.”

So my anxiety, reflection, and anger toward my father and what I had heard from him increased, and I pressed him further about his conduct and what he had said concerning him. After that, I had no concern except asking about his reports and investigating his matter. I did not ask anyone among Banu Hashim, the commanders, the scribes, the judges, the jurists, or the rest of the people, except that I found him held by them in the utmost reverence, magnification, lofty station, and beautiful mention, and preferred over all his household and elders. Thus his standing grew great in my eyes, since I saw neither friend nor enemy of his except that he spoke well of him and praised him.

Then one of those present in his gathering from the Ash'aris said to him, “O Abu Bakr, what about the news of his brother Ja'far?” He said, “And who is Ja'far, that one should ask about his report or compare him with al-Hasan? Ja'far is one who openly displays sinfulness, wicked, licentious, addicted to wine, the least of men I have seen, and the most disgraceful toward himself—frivolous and insignificant in his own person.”

There occurred before the ruler and his associates, at the time of the death of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, something at which I was astonished and had not expected to happen. That was when he fell ill and word was sent to my father that Ibn al-Rida had become ill. My father immediately mounted and hastened to the court of the caliphate, then returned quickly with five of the servants of Amir al-Mu'minin, all of them among his trusted and close attendants; among them was Nahriir.

He ordered them to remain at the house of al-Hasan and ascertain his condition and state. He also sent for a group of physicians and ordered them to come and go to him and attend to him morning and evening. Then, two or three days later, when he was informed that he had grown weaker, he ordered the physicians to remain at his house, and he sent for the chief judge, had him brought to his assembly, and ordered him to select ten of his companions who were trusted in religion, trustworthiness, and scrupulousness. He brought them, and he sent them to the house of al-Hasan and ordered them to remain with him night and day.

They remained there until he passed away, peace be upon him, and Surra Man Ra'a became one great outcry. The ruler sent people to his house to search it and its rooms, and he sealed all that was in it. They sought traces of his son, and they brought women who recognized signs of pregnancy. They entered upon his slave-women and examined them, and one of them mentioned that there was a slave-girl who appeared to be pregnant. She was then placed in a room, and Nahriir the servant, his companions, and some women were assigned to her.

Then after that they proceeded with preparing him, and the markets were shut down. Banu Hashim, the commanders, my father, and the rest of the people rode out to his funeral, and Surra Man Ra'a on that day resembled the Day of Resurrection. When they had finished preparing him, the ruler sent for Abu 'Isa ibn al-Mutawakkil and ordered him to perform the salat (prayer) over him.

When the bier was placed for the salat (prayer) over him, Abu 'Isa approached, uncovered his face, and displayed him to Banu Hashim among the 'Alawis and the 'Abbasids, the commanders, the scribes, the judges, and the official witnesses. He said, “This is al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Rida. He died a natural death on his bed.”

Those present with him from the servants of Amir al-Mu'minin and his trusted men were so-and-so and so-and-so; from the judges, so-and-so and so-and-so; and from the physicians, so-and-so and so-and-so. Then he covered his face, ordered that he be carried, and he was carried from the middle of his house and buried in the house in which his father had been buried.

When he had been buried, the ruler and the people began seeking his son, and searching in homes and houses became extensive. They halted the division of his inheritance, and those assigned to guard the slave-girl upon whom pregnancy had been suspected remained with her until the falsity of the pregnancy became clear. When the pregnancy claim was nullified, his inheritance was divided between his mother and his brother Ja'far. His mother claimed his bequest, and that was established before the judge, while the ruler still continued seeking traces of his son.

After that, Ja'far came to my father and said, “Assign to me the rank of my brother, and I will deliver to you twenty thousand dinars every year.” My father rebuked him harshly and said to him, “O fool, the ruler unsheathed his sword against those who claimed that your father and your brother are Imams, to turn them away from that, yet he was unable to do so. If you are an Imam in the eyes of the Shi'ah of your father or your brother, then you have no need of the ruler—or anyone other than the ruler—to assign you their ranks; and if you do not have this standing among them, you will not attain it through us.” My father then regarded him as insignificant and weak, and ordered that he be barred from him. He never permitted him to enter upon him until my father died, and we departed while he remained in that condition, and the ruler was still seeking traces of the son of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali.

key_terms.إِمَامُ الرَّافِضَةِ: the leader recognized by the Shi'ah community
key_terms.النَّصْبِ: hostility toward Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: the divinely guided leadership claimed for the Imam
key_terms.الْعَلَوِيَّةِ: the 'Alawis, the descendants or partisans associated with Imam 'Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْعِبَادَةِ: devotional worship and servitude to Allah
key_terms.مِيرَاثِهِ: his inheritance and estate after death
key_terms.وَلَدِهِ: his son, whose trace the authorities sought

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith portray the public stature of Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari عليه السلام and the Abbasid reaction to his death?
ai.summary: This report describes the extraordinary reverence shown by state officials and the wider public toward al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-'Askari عليه السلام, even by those hostile to the 'Alawis. It also records the intense political scrutiny surrounding his final illness, death, funeral, inheritance, and the search for his son, highlighting his recognized stature and the anxiety of the Abbasid state regarding the Imamate.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary and Muhammad Bin yahya and some others who said,

‘It was so that Ahmad Bin Ubeydullah Bin Khaqan was in charge of the estates and the taxes at Qumm, and one day the discussion flowed in this gathering of the Alawites and their doctrines, and he used to be intensely hostile (Nasibi). So he said, ‘I have not seen nor do I recognise in Surmanrayy (Samarrah) a man from the Alawites the like of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>, regarding his<sup>asws</sup> Guidance, and his<sup>asws</sup> tranquillity, and his<sup>asws</sup> piety, and his<sup>asws</sup> nobility, and his<sup>asws</sup> benevolence in the presence of his<sup>asws</sup> family and the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>, and their preferring him<sup>asws</sup> upon the ones with age from them, and the officials, and similar to that, the leaders, and the ministers and the generality of the people’.

So, one day I was standing by the head of my father, and it was the day of his (Khaqan’s) gathering to the people, when his guards came over to him and they said, ‘Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> is at the door. So he said at the top of this voice, ‘There is permission for him<sup>asws</sup>!’ So I was astounded from what I had heard from them. They had been audacious to teknonym a man upon my father in his presence, and it did not happen in his presence except for a Caliph or a crown prince, or the one for whom the Sultan would have ordered that he be teknonymed.

So there entered a brown man of good stature, beautiful of face, good of the body (physically), young of age. For him<sup>asws</sup> was majesty and awe. So when my father looked at him, he stood up to walk towards him barefooted, and I had not known him do this with anyone from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup> and the leaders. So when he went near him<sup>asws</sup>, he hugged him<sup>asws</sup> and kissed his<sup>asws</sup> face and his<sup>asws</sup> chest, and grabbed his<sup>asws</sup> hand and seated him<sup>asws</sup> upon his Prayer mat which he had been seated upon, and he sat by his side, facing towards him<sup>asws</sup>, and went on to speak to him<sup>asws</sup>, and ransoming himself.

And I was astonished from what I saw from him. When the guard entered and said, ‘Al-Mowaffaq has come’, and it was so that Al-Mowaffaq, whenever he came over to my father, his guards and his officials would precede him, and they would be sitting between my father’s seat and the door of the house of Simatayn until he would enter and exit. But my father did not cease to face Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> discussing with him<sup>asws</sup> until he looked at the special attendants, so he said, ‘Then, whenever you<sup>asws</sup> so desire to (leave), may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’

Then he said to his guards, ‘Go with himasws behind Al-Simateyn until this one, meaning Al-Mowaffaq, does not see himasws. So heasws stood and my father stood and hugged himasws, and heasws went away. So I said to the guards of my father and his attendants, ‘Woe unto you all! Who is this one whom you teknonymed upon my father and my father did with himasws this deed?’ So they said, ‘This is an Alawite called Al-Hassanasws Bin Aliasws, well knowns as the sonasws of Al-Rezaasws. So it increased my astonishment and it did not cease during that day of mine being uneasy, thinking regarding hisasws affair and the affair of my father and what I saw with regards to it until it was the night, and it was his habit that he used to pray the Isha Salat, then he would sit looking into what would be needy to from the matter (of the state) and what (matters) he would be raising to the Sultan.

So when he had prayed Salat and was seated, I went over and sat in front of him, and there wasn’t anyone (else) in his presence. So he said to me, ‘O Ahmad! For you there is a need?’ I said, ‘Yes, O father, so if you would allow me, I shall ask you about it’. So he said, ‘I have permitted to you, O my son, so say whatever you like’. I said, ‘O father! Who was that man whom I saw in the morning? You dealt with himasws what you dealt with from the majesty, and the prestige, and the reverence, and you were ransoming yourself and your parents’.

So he said, ‘O my son! That is the Imam<sup>asws</sup> of the Rafiziites (rejecters). That is Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, well known as the son<sup>asws</sup> of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>’. So he was silent for a while, then he said, ‘O my son! If the leadership were to decline from the Caliphs of the Clan of Abbas, no one from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup> would be rightful for it apart from this one, and that this one is rightful for it due to his<sup>asws</sup> merits, and his<sup>asws</sup> chastity, and his<sup>asws</sup> Guidance, and his<sup>asws</sup> infallibility, and his<sup>asws</sup> ascetism, and his<sup>asws</sup> worship, and the beauty of his<sup>asws</sup> morals, and his<sup>asws</sup> correctness. And had you seen his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, you would have seen a man intelligent, noble, meritorious’.

So it increased my uneasiness, and thinking, and rage upon my father and what I heard from him, and he had increased in his deed and his words with regards to him<sup>asws</sup>, what he said. So there did not happen to be any mettle for me after that except the asking about his<sup>asws</sup> news and the discussion about his<sup>asws</sup> matter. So I did not ask anyone from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>, and leaders, and the scribes, and the judges, and the jurists and the rest of the people except that I found him<sup>asws</sup> in his presence to be at the peak of the majesty and the magnificence, and the lofty position, and the beautiful words, and the preference for him unto the entirety of his<sup>asws</sup> family, and his<sup>asws</sup> elders. So that magnified his<sup>asws</sup> worth in my presence when I did not see a friend of his<sup>asws</sup> nor an enemy except he would good with the words regarding him<sup>asws</sup>, and the praises upon him<sup>asws</sup>.

So one of those who were present in his (my father’s) gathering, from the Ashariites asked him, ‘O Abu Bakr! So what is the news of his<sup>asws</sup> brother Ja’far?’ So he said, ‘And who is Ja’far, that you are asking of his news? O are you supporting Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, or Ja’far the accursed, the transgressor, the immoral, an addict of drinking the wine, the lowest of the ones I have seen from the men, and the disgraceful to himself, a light and less with regards to himself?

And there had been referred upon the Sultan and his companions during the time of the passing away of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> what I was astounded from, and I did not think it would be happening, and that is that when he<sup>asws</sup> fell ill, he sent a message to my father that the son<sup>asws</sup> of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> has fallen ill. So he rode immediately and went to the house of the Caliphate. Then he returned in a jury and with him were five from the attendants of the commander of the faithful, all of them being from his reliable ones and his special ones, among them being Niheyr.

So he (my father) ordered them with staying at the door of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and get to know his<sup>asws</sup> news and his<sup>asws</sup> state. And he sent a message to a number of the physicians and ordered them with the coming and going to him<sup>asws</sup>, and to see him<sup>asws</sup> morning and evening. So when it was after that by two days or three, he was informed that he<sup>asws</sup> had weakened. So he ordered the physicians with the staying at his<sup>asws</sup> house, and sent a message to the Chief Justice to be present in his gathering and ordered him that he chooses ten from his companions, from the one he could rely with regards to his religion, and his entrustments, and his piety. So he presented them and sent them to the door of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and instructed them of staying there day and night.

So they did not cease to be over these until he<sup>asws</sup> passed away. So Surmanrayy (Samarrah) became one sensation, and the Sultan sent to his<sup>asws</sup> house the one who would investigate him<sup>asws</sup> and investigate his<sup>asws</sup> chambers, and he<sup>asws</sup> sealed off upon the entirety of whatever was in it, and they sought the traces of his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> (12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and they came with women for them to recognise any pregnancy (that may be). So these women went over to his<sup>asws</sup> maids looking at them, and one of them mentioned that over there is a maid who could be expecting. So she was made to be in a room and Niheyr the servant and his companions were allocated with her, and the women were with them.

Then after that, they took to the preparation (for hisasws funeral), and the markets were closed, and the Clan of Hashimas, and the officials, and my father, and the rest of the people rode to hisasws funeral. So it was as if Surmanrayy (Samarrah) in that day resembled the day of Judgment. So when they were free from hisasws preparation, the Sultan sent a message to Abu Isa Bin Al-Mutawakil and ordered him with the (leading of the) Salat upon himasws.

So when the body was placed for the Salat to be prayed upon himasws, Abu Isa approached it, and he uncovered from hisasws face and he displayed it to the Clan of Hashimas, from the Alawites and the Abbasides, and the officials, and the scribes, and the judges, and the juries and said, ‘This is Al-Hassanasws Bin Aliasws Bin Muhammadasws Bin Al-Rezaasws! Heasws passed away a natural death upon hisasws bed’.

He attended it, the one who attended it, from the servants of the commander of the faithful, and his trusted ones were so and so, and so and so, and from the judges were so and so and so and so, and from the physicians were so and so and so and so. Then he covered his<sup>asws</sup> face and instructed with him<sup>asws</sup> to be carried from the middle of his<sup>asws</sup> house and to be buried in the room in which his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was buried in.

So when he<sup>asws</sup> was buried, the Sultan and the people took to seeking his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> (12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and there was a lot of investigation in the houses and the rooms, and there was a stop to the distribution of his<sup>asws</sup> inheritance, and those who had been allocated with the protection of the (pregnant) slave girl did not cease to be suspicious upon her of the pregnancy, staying with her until it became clear that the claim of the pregnancy was invalid about her. His<sup>asws</sup> inheritance was distributed between his<sup>asws</sup> mother, and his<sup>asws</sup> brother Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. And his<sup>asws</sup> mother claimed to be his<sup>asws</sup> executor of the will, and that was affirmed in the presence of the judge, and the Sultan, on top of that, sought the traces of his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> (12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>).

So Ja’far came over after that to my father and he said, ‘Make for me the status of my brother<sup>asws</sup> to be for me, and I shall send to you twenty thousand Dinars every year. But my father rebuked him and made him hear (harsh words) and said to him, ‘O idiot! The Sultan has bared his sword regarding those who are claiming that your father<sup>asws</sup> and your brother<sup>asws</sup> are Imams<sup>asws</sup>, in order to return them from that, so why are you preparing that for him? So if you were an Imam<sup>asws</sup> in the presence of the Shias of your father<sup>asws</sup> and your brother<sup>asws</sup>, then there would be no need for you to the Sultan that he should give you their<sup>asws</sup> status, nor for anyone other than the Sultan (to do so), and if you do not happen to be an Imam<sup>asws</sup> in their<sup>asws</sup> presence with this status, why would you need it with us?’ And my father belittled him during that and weakened him and ordered that he be blocked from him. So he was not allowed to come over to him until my father died, and we went out and he was upon that state, and the Sultan was (still) seeking the traces of the son<sup>asws</sup> of Al-Hassan Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: Abu Muhammad al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.) was born in the month of Ramadan (in an other copy it is in ‘the month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal) in the year two hundred thirty two. He died on a Friday on the eighth of the month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal in the year two hundred sixty at the age of twenty eight.
He was buried in the house where his father was buried in the city of Surra man Ra‘a (Samarra).her was ’Umm Walad, called Hudayth (or Sawsan).
